01 Real subscription checks

These are version-specific evidence records and procedures, not a claim that every later build was tested. For current installed readiness, run gateway rollout --verify --json. Return to the verification overview.

Real subscription checks

On October 13 a development gateway on the native-spend build forwarded the Codex 2 turn-state through a real two-turn Codex CLI 0.160 run (GPT-5.6-Luna, low effort). With a 2-second cap on the deferred response head, the second turn lost its turn-state: upstream heads took 1.5 to 4.7 seconds, and 6 of 10 eligible requests opened their head without the header. With the head waiting up to one heartbeat interval, all four head probes (1.9 to 3.2 seconds) carried the header, and each turn returned a turn-state on its first request and echoed it on the next. The probe recorded only timings, booleans and token counts.

MacBook Pro 2 passed a real Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Codex 2 GPT-6.1-Sol loop over an authenticated SSH forward. It streamed text and reasoning, read a random file proof, applied a dedicated patch, retained follow-up history, switched providers, acknowledged cancellation, released its worker, and completed a recovery turn. Only the gateway client token crossed SSH. Provider credentials stayed on the inference host.

Copilot CLI 1.0.95 passed the real bundled Codex loop on MacBook Pro 2 through SDK protocol 3: incremental text, file proof, custom patch and verification, follow-up replay, provider-exposed reasoning, interruption, worker cleanup, and recovery. Interruption was acknowledged in 3 ms. Earlier discovery returned 13 explicitly selectable models after removing Auto. The current catalog exposes only the four requested Copilot models. This test proves one model's full loop, not every discovered model's inference access. Rendered Copilot selection remains unverified.

Copilot live sessions (copilotSessions.mode: "live") passed a real check on CLI 1.0.97 in October 2026, through an isolated test gateway with its own state folder and TMPDIR, on gpt-6-luna. A three-round tool loop stayed in one CLI process. Rounds 2 and 3 read 98% of their input from the cache, wrote under 60 tokens and cost 4.8 to 6.0 million nano-AIU each. An effort change between turns continued the same session with 98.6% read from the cache. Stop while a tool waited reseeded the thread (unexpected_tail), and a request without a thread id ran one-shot. Every request wrote one content-free ledger row with complete credit figures. ~/.copilot gained no session rows or session folders. A normal shutdown removed the parked session's process and folder. After the gateway was killed outright, its CLIs exited when their input closed, and the next gateway's startup sweep removed their folders. The check found that the CLI sends session.idle right after assistant.idle; the gateway first treated it as unrequested output, and now accepts it between requests. That check did not cover a one-shot request that ends in tool calls on the external-tool setup, which the gateway closes with session.abort and SIGKILL as a live session ends; only the scripted CLI fixture tests cover it, so repeat it against the installed CLI after upgrading.

A real text sweep passed all 20 loaded Claude/Codex 2 routes. It found and verified a fix for the unsupported upstream summary: "none" value. Copilot passed 12 of 13 routes in that earlier catalog. Its Opus 5 request returned Opus 4.8, so the gateway rejected the substitution. That route is not verified as usable. The Copilot Sol 6.1 catalog also advertised none, which its endpoint rejected; discovery now omits that unsupported effort. These sweeps do not prove images or every model's tool loop. Run node scripts/e2e-models.mjs --config PATH --output PATH to repeat them.

All 20 Claude/Codex 2 routes passed a real PNG check whose random eight-digit code appeared only in pixels. Sonnet 5.5 and Codex 2 Sol also passed JPEG, WebP, and GIF checks with follow-ups and image tool-result replay. Copilot Sonnet 5.5 and Luna passed PNG input, follow-up, and tool-result checks.

The bundled Codex engine on MacBook Pro 2 passed four operations for each of the 20 Claude/Codex 2 models: local image attachment, turn interruption, saved-chat resume after restarting the engine, and real view_image execution. Each model read the correct picture code. This verifies the engine and transport, not the rendered attachment UI. Codex's tested pause behavior interrupts a turn and starts a new turn from saved history; it does not suspend and continue the same token stream.

scripts/e2e-images.mjs runs direct image checks. Its fixture directory contains fixture.png and any selected fixture.jpg, fixture.gif, or fixture.webp, plus expected.json with code, colors, and shapes. scripts/e2e-agent-images.mjs runs attachment, stop/resume, and viewer checks through the real bundled engine. scripts/e2e-all-tools.mjs repeats the file-read/edit, follow-up, reasoning, cancellation, and recovery loop for every configured alias. Models without a reasoning capability report that case unsupported rather than inventing reasoning.

The complete file/tool sweep passed all 20 Claude/Codex 2 aliases: streamed text, random file proof, native patch and verification, follow-up replay, supported reasoning, interruption, worker cleanup, and recovery. Daybreak added a final period to the recovery marker; the checker now accepts terminal punctuation and its full loop passed again. Copilot CLI 1.0.91 repeated its entire model catalog. Discovery removes identical repetitions and rejects conflicting metadata for the same ID. The account is not switched and its CLI is not updated automatically. That CLI also omits the optional assistant providerId. The adapter accepts its response only after subscription usage reports isByok: false and the returned model matches the request. Explicit provider changes and BYOK still fail closed.

Earlier bundled-engine checks on the inference host verified the primary account and the then-current 28-model catalog. A separate Haiku 4.5 request verified its no-reasoning route. Listing a model does not prove inference access or inclusion without usage credits. Native inference has not been tested for every native account model.
